record.paper_title: On two open problems on the normality of bent functions
record.original_question: Does there exist a non-normal Boolean bent function in 8 variables whose algebraic degree is 4?

evidence.quote: Do non-normal bent functions in 8 variables and degree 4 exist?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Boolean function in $n$ variables is a map $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n \to \mathbb{F}_2$. Its Walsh-Hadamard transform is $W_f(a) = \sum_{x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n}(-1)^{f(x)+a\cdot x}$ for $a\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. The function $f$ is called bent if $|W_f(a)| = 2^{n/2}$ for every $a\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$ (which requires $n$ to be even). The algebraic degree of $f$ is the degree of its (unique) algebraic normal form as a multilinear polynomial over $\mathbb{F}_2$. A Boolean function $f$ in $n$ variables (with $n$ even) is called normal if there exists an $(n/2)$-dimensional affine subspace $V \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ on which $f$ is constant; otherwise $f$ is called non-normal.

Question: Does there exist a non-normal Boolean bent function in $8$ variables whose algebraic degree equals $4$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question has been answered affirmatively. A non-normal bent function in 8 variables of algebraic degree 4 was constructed (within the partial spread class) and presented by Polujan, Mariot and Picek, with further work appearing in arXiv preprints "On the Normality of Boolean quartics" (2407.14038) and "Normality of 8-bit bent functions" (2504.21779).

status_evidence.title: On the Normality of Boolean quartics
status_evidence.snippet: First example of a non-normal bent quartic in 8 variables, belonging to the partial spread class.
status_evidence.claim: A non-normal bent function in 8 variables of degree 4 exists.

status_evidence.title: Normality of 8-bit bent functions
status_evidence.snippet: Studies normality of bent functions in 8 variables, including non-normal degree-4 examples.
status_evidence.claim: Non-normal bent functions of degree 4 in 8 variables are exhibited and analyzed.
